name: x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI (vpermi2b, vpermb -- key base64 enablers)
description: The game-changing instruction subset for base64. VPERMB enables single-instruction 64-byte cross-lane byte permutation; VPMULTISHIFTQB enables single-instruction multi-field extraction. Together they reduce the decode pipeline from ~12 instructions to ~6.

key_instructions.purpose: Full 64-byte cross-lane byte permutation in ONE instruction. Replaces vpshufb+vpermq cascade. Used for (1) input->6-bit LUT lookup and (2) output byte compaction.
key_instructions.note: Ice Lake: 3c lat is excellent. Zen4: 6c lat is higher but still 1 CPI throughput.

key_instructions.purpose: Byte permutation from TWO source registers (128-byte combined table). Could enable full Base64 decode lookup from a single instruction with 128-entry table.
key_instructions.note: CRITICAL: 3 uops on Intel (2 CPI) vs 1 uop on Zen4 (1 CPI). Algorithm choice depends on target microarchitecture.

key_instructions.purpose: Extracts 8 arbitrary-positioned 8-bit fields from each 64-bit qword. THE key instruction for base64 packing: extracts packed 6-bit fields without shift/mask chains. One instruction replaces ~4 shift+AND+OR operations.
key_instructions.note: Remarkably efficient on both Intel and AMD. Single uop, 3c latency.

base64_applicability: The optimal decode pipeline with VBMI: (1) vpermb for LUT lookup (1 instr, replaces 3 vpshufb + comparisons), (2) vpmultishiftqb for 6-bit field extraction/packing (1 instr, replaces vpmaddubsw + vpmaddwd), (3) vpermb for output compaction (1 instr, replaces vpshufb + vpermq). Total: ~6 core instructions vs ~12 for AVX2. Mula/Lemire achieve near-memcpy throughput with this pipeline.
hardware_availability: Ice Lake (2019), Tiger Lake (2020), Alder Lake (2021 E-cores only), Sapphire Rapids (2023), Emerald Rapids (2024), Zen4 (2022), Zen5 (2024). Increasingly available but not universal.
